item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem:
The figure represents two similar triangles. The triangles are not drawn to scale.

[Image: Triangles ABC and DEF]

In the actual triangle ABC, what is the length of side BC?
item.figure_description:
Two right triangles are shown side by side:
- On the left is triangle ABC: vertical leg AB on the left, horizontal base BC on the bottom, with vertex B at the right-angle corner. Hypotenuse AC is labeled "6 cm". Inside angle A is labeled "50°" and inside angle C is labeled "40°".
- On the right is a larger triangle DEF: vertical leg DE on the left, horizontal base EF on the bottom labeled "15 cm", with vertex E at the right-angle corner. Hypotenuse DF is labeled "20 cm". Inside angle D is labeled "50°" and inside angle F is labeled "40°".
item.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.stem:
In this figure, triangles ABC and DEF are congruent with BC = EF .

[Image: Overlapping triangles ABC and DEF]

What is the measure of angle EGC ?
reference_items.figure_description: Two overlapping triangles, ABC and DEF, resting on a shared horizontal baseline containing points B, E, C, and F in that order from left to right. Segment BC is the base of triangle ABC, and segment EF is the base of triangle DEF. Vertex A is above the baseline, and vertex D is to the right of A and also above the baseline. Side AC intersects side DE at point G. Angle B is labeled 40°, and angle F is labeled 60°.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Two of the triangles below are similar.

[Image: Four triangles labeled I, II, III, IV]

Which two triangles are similar?
reference_items.figure_description:
Four triangles displayed side by side:
- Triangle I: A scalene obtuse triangle with a horizontal base at the bottom. The top vertex is closer to the left, so the left side is shorter than the right side.
- Triangle II: An acute isosceles triangle with a horizontal top edge. The two longer sides point downward to meet at a sharp vertex at the bottom.
- Triangle III: A tall, thin obtuse triangle with a short horizontal base at the bottom. The left side slants steeply upward to a top vertex, which connects via a long hypotenuse-like side down to the right end of the base.
- Triangle IV: A scalene obtuse triangle with a horizontal top edge, pointing downward to a vertex at the bottom offset to the right. It has the same shape and internal angles as Triangle I, but rotated 180° and reduced in size.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: Large right triangle divided into smaller triangles]

In the figure above, each of the smaller triangles has the same area. What is the ratio of the shaded area to the unshaded area?
reference_items.figure_description:
A large right triangle with its vertical leg on the left and horizontal leg at the bottom, divided into smaller congruent right triangles arranged in 4 horizontal rows and 4 vertical columns:
- Row 4 (top): Column 1 contains 1 shaded right triangle with its right angle at the bottom-left and its hypotenuse along the hypotenuse of the large triangle.
- Row 3: Column 1 contains a rectangle divided by a diagonal into a shaded triangle (bottom-left) and an unshaded triangle (top-right); Column 2 contains 1 shaded right triangle with its hypotenuse along the large triangle's hypotenuse.
- Row 2: Columns 1 and 2 each contain a rectangle divided by a diagonal into a shaded triangle (bottom-left) and an unshaded triangle (top-right); Column 3 contains 1 shaded right triangle with its hypotenuse along the large triangle's hypotenuse.
- Row 1 (bottom): Columns 1, 2, and 3 each contain a rectangle divided by a diagonal into a shaded triangle (bottom-left) and an unshaded triangle (top-right); Column 4 contains 1 shaded right triangle with its hypotenuse along the large triangle's hypotenuse.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: A large triangle. The left angle is 45 degrees and the top angle is 65 degrees. A line is drawn on the side between the 45 and 64 degree angle to form two smaller triangles—one adjacent to the larger triangle, and one contained within the larger triangle. The right most angle of the triangle adjacent to the larger triangle has an angle of 30 degrees. The smaller triangle contained within the bigger triangle has an angle x that is formed by the right side of the triangle and the drawn line.]

In the figure above, what is the value of x?
reference_items.figure_description: A geometric figure featuring intersecting lines and triangles. A triangle has a horizontal base, a left side with an interior angle of 45° at the bottom-left vertex, and an interior angle of 65° at the top vertex. A line segment extends from the top vertex down to the base. A second line segment extends from a point on the left side of the triangle down and to the right, crossing the first line segment and ending at the rightmost endpoint of the extended horizontal base, where the interior angle is labeled 30°. Near the top vertex, a smaller triangle is bounded by the upper part of the left side, the upper part of the segment from the top vertex, and the crossing segment; the interior angle at the intersection of the two segments is marked with an arc and labeled x.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data.

options.label: A

reference_items.figure_description:
Four options showing visual representations:
- Option A shows a horizontal line segment with vertical tick marks at its ends, divided into two segments by an interior vertical tick mark. The segment on the left is labeled x above, and the segment on the right is labeled 5 above.
- Option B shows a horizontal line segment with vertical tick marks at its ends, divided into three segments by two interior vertical tick marks. From left to right, the segments are labeled 2, 3, and x above.
- Option C shows a rectangle with its left vertical side labeled x. A vertical dotted line extends through the rectangle, dividing the top horizontal side into two parts, labeled 2 on the left and 3 on the right.
- Option D shows a rectangle with its left vertical side labeled 5. A vertical dotted line extends through the rectangle, dividing the top horizontal side into two equal parts, each labeled x above.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration.
